title: xo github issues — the runtime mirror of one repo's issues
description: The GitHub issue mirror for one project, at ~/.quirq/projects/<pid>/github/issues.json (workitems-plan.md §5.2). RUNTIME TIER, never .xo/: it is re-fetched every 60 s and rebuilt from scratch after `rm -rf ~/.quirq`, so R-TIER puts it outside the synced tree and A10 cannot be violated by it. Wholly owned by the poller, which is the single writer — hence write_json_atomic_if_changed rather than a key-scoped merge, and hence a corrupt file is repaired by overwriting rather than merged into. Keyed by `node_id` because a union key must be unique BY CONSTRUCTION (§2, the O-C lesson): `number` is per-repo and would collide across repos, and a repo rename changes the URL but never the node id. The document is a cache and states so: everything in it is authoritative on GitHub, nothing in it is authored, and losing it costs one poll.

repo.description: `owner/name`, parsed from project.json:git.remote_url by connectors/github_issues.parse_remote_url(). Recorded so a mirror can never be read as belonging to a repo it did not come from — the remote can change under a project.

fetched_at.description: When the poll that produced this document completed, UTC. Null only on a document written before any poll has succeeded. The UI's staleness indicator reads this, not `since`.

since.description: High-water mark (§6.3): the `updatedAt` of the most recently updated issue this document has seen, fed back as filterBy.since so a quiet repo settles into a small response. It does NOT reduce the query's point cost (measured: still 1) — it reduces payload, not budget.

rate.description: GraphQL rate-limit state as of the last poll, read from the `rateLimit` field inside the query itself. That source is deliberate: `gh api rate_limit` was measured returning a full budget regardless of consumption on a real token, and the inline field costs no extra call. Null when unknown — after an auth failure there is no budget to report, and a fabricated one is worse than none.

limit.description: Points per hour on the GraphQL budget: 5000. Separate from the REST 5000/hr, which this poll does not touch at all (§6.2).

cost.description: Points the last poll spent. 1 for the pinned query; 2 would mean a nested connection was added and the ~83-repo ceiling has halved.

reset_at.description: When the budget refills. The backoff honours this instead of guessing.

error.description: The last poll failure, or null after a poll that succeeded. Structured rather than a bare string because the UI has to tell apart states with different remedies: `not_authenticated` asks the user to connect GitHub, `not_found` says the repo is gone, `network` says wait. `kind` is the closed vocabulary in connectors/github_issues.ERROR_KINDS, so an unrecognised state fails here instead of reaching the UI as an unhandled string.

message.description: Human-readable, and safe to display: it is composed from gh's own text, which never contains the token.

issues.description: Map of node_id → issue snapshot. Pull requests are structurally impossible here: `gh` reads GraphQL, where repository.issues and repository.pullRequests are separate connections (§6.1). The REST /issues endpoint does return PRs, which is one of the reasons D5 chose gh.

node_id.description: GitHub's global node id, and the map key. Survives a repo rename or transfer, which `number` does too but the URL does not; adopted workitems match on this (§5.1).

number.description: The human handle. Unique within a repo only — never used as a map key.

state.description: Lowercased from GraphQL's OPEN/CLOSED. Exactly GitHub's two values and no others (§5.4, D7): a vocabulary we do not own cannot drift from GitHub's, and `in_progress` is derived from a live claim rather than stored anywhere.

state_reason.description: Lowercased from GraphQL's stateReason. `closed` + `not_planned` is what 'cancelled' means here — mirrored from GitHub, not invented.

assignees.description: Who GitHub has on the issue. This was THE coordination substrate under D1 — assignment WAS a GitHub assignee — and that decision was reversed (workitems-plan §13, amendment 33): nothing in this system writes an assignee any more, so this array is information about the issue rather than an assignment made here. It is still fetched, and still matters: it is the only way a peer's claim on an issue reaches this machine, so the projection serves it as `github_assignees` beside the workitem's own `assignee` and the rollup matches both. Costs nothing extra — assignees(first:5) measured at 1 point, the same as omitting it. An empty array means nobody is on it upstream; the field's absence means the row was written by something that is not the poller.

labels.description: OPTIONAL, and absent on every row the poller writes. labels(first:10) was measured to double the query cost from 1 to 2, halving the ceiling from ~83 polled repos to ~41 (§6.2), so labels are fetched lazily on adoption instead. Absent means 'not fetched'; an empty array would be the claim 'this issue has no labels', which the poll never establishes.

url.description: Always .../issues/<number> — GraphQL's Issue.url. A /pull/ URL here would mean the query stopped being an issues query.

updated_at.description: GitHub's updatedAt, verbatim. Drives the high-water mark and the sort.
